title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor-Train Accelerated Split Bregman for Boundary Detection in Large Aerial Images
content: We propose a quantum-inspired tensor-train (QTT) accelerated Split Bregman method for boundary detection in aerospace remote sensing images, addressing the challenges of weak contrast, complex topology, and ultra-high resolution that compromise accuracy and scalability. The method builds on the Split Bregman iteration for solving a convexly relaxed Chan-Vese model. Images and discrete difference operators are represented via bit-interleaved binary encoding as low-rank QTT-MPS states and MPO chains with bond dimension as low as 6, respectively. Combined with randomized SVD right-hand side mapping, AMEn variational sweeping, and half-edge kernel contraction reconstruction, the per-iteration complexity is reduced from \( \mathcal{O}(N^2\log N) \) to \( \mathcal{O}(\log_2(N^2)\cdot\chi^3) \). We prove that the inexact iteration converges strongly to a saddle-point optimal solution set when the inner truncation errors satisfy a summability condition. Numerical experiments show that the QTT format achieves a compression ratio of 7581.2× at 8192 × 8192 resolution, demonstrates boundary fidelity on real satellite images of 16384 × 16384. This offers a scalable and robust new route for boundary detection in large aerospace remote sensing imagery.
